item.content:encoded:
AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-11-13

Generated: 2026-11-13 01:46 UTC | Tools covered: 7

  • Claude Code
  • OpenAI Codex
  • Gemini CLI
  • GitHub Copilot CLI
  • OpenCode
  • Pi
  • Qwen Code
  • Claude Code Skills

Cross-Tool Comparison

Cross-Tool Community Comparison Report — 2026-11-13

Scope: Claude Code · OpenAI Codex · Gemini CLI · GitHub Copilot CLI · OpenCode · Pi · Qwen Code

1. Ecosystem Overview

The AI CLI ecosystem is now a mature, multi-polar market with at least seven credible contenders, each iterating on a weekly cadence. The competitive frontier has shifted from raw model capability to agent runtime robustness: subagent lifecycle, checkpointing, sandboxing, tool dispatch correctness, and auth/MCP plumbing now dominate issue trackers. Simultaneously, a convergence on agentic architecture is visible — Code Mode (Claude Code), event-driven loop kernels (Qwen Code), the Advisor dual-model tool (OpenCode), and agent-tree suspension (Codex) all point toward the same destination: multi-agent, resumable, tool-rich sessions. Meanwhile, platform-specific friction (Windows, WSL, Wayland, tmux/screen, headless Linux) has become a first-order source of user pain. Underneath the polish, every project is fighting the same physics: context budgets, MCP authentication, and resource leaks in long-lived processes.

2. Activity Comparison

Tool Issues (hot/active today) PRs (updated 24h) Discussions Release Status (24h)
Claude Code 10+ highlighted; heavy filing 1 open (stale since July) Omitted (no data provided) ✅ v2.1.323 (Code Mode, plugin engines)
OpenAI Codex 10 highlighted + 3 closed ~13 closed (all merged/resolved) ✅ 8 active (Ideas, Q&A) ✅ 2 alphas (rust-v0.170.0-alpha.3/.4)
Gemini CLI 10 highlighted 10 active (2 closed) Omitted (no data provided) ❌ None
GitHub Copilot CLI 10 highlighted 0 Omitted (no data provided) ✅ v1.0.110 (password helper, Entra polish)
OpenCode 10 highlighted ~11 active (1 closed) Omitted (no data provided) ❌ None
Pi 10 highlighted (many closing) 10 (mostly closed) Omitted (no data provided) ❌ None
Qwen Code 10 highlighted ~10 active Omitted (no data provided) ✅ 5 releases (v0.27.3 + v1.0.0-preview.1 + SDK + Desktop + nightly)

Reading the table: Copilot CLI's zero-PR day is stark given its large user base — community momentum is entirely issue-side this cycle. Codex shows the most aggressive merge velocity (~13 PRs closed in 24h), while Qwen Code shows the most aggressive release velocity (five artifacts in one day, including the 1.0 preview). Claude Code's near-total absence of PR activity (1 stale PR) is unusual for a repo of its scale and suggests either a maintainer-gated contribution model or backlog pressure. Note: Discussions sections marked "Omitted" reflect the absence of data in the source feeds, not necessarily zero activity; absence of a Discussions channel in a repo is a configuration fact, not evidence of inactivity.

3. Shared Feature Directions

Five requirements recurring across three or more tool communities:

1. Session/workspace continuity & resumability

  • Codex: workspace-scoped chats (#25319, top-voted), thread-input preservation across resumes (#61216), safe checkpointing at usage limits (#60447)
  • Claude Code: mid-session re-login killing background subagents (#108585)
  • Pi: /resume selection stability (#12111), kill-on-quit zombie processes (#12107)
  • Qwen Code: resume interrupted turns on session load (#16528)
  • OpenCode: "Advisor" and cross-session hooks (#63637, #63590)

2. Safe checkpointing / graceful degradation under resource limits

  • Codex: terminate without safe checkpoint (#60447, explicit "19 files modified, tests passing, then killed" scenario)
  • Pi: ENOSPC/EACCES on /tmp crashing whole process (#10585)
  • Copilot CLI: OOM crashes in long sessions (#5435), event-store exhaustion (#4467)
  • OpenCode: long turns dying mid-stream with ECONNRESET (#60940)
  • Qwen Code: ACP child idle-unresponsive after network calls (#17040)

3. MCP authentication & lifecycle maturity

  • Copilot CLI: Entra broker cache (#5236), Google Workspace OAuth (#4606), OAuth in delegated children (#5437)
  • Pi: Google MCP refresh tokens requiring access_type=offline (#10563)
  • Codex: SSPI/OAuth metadata handling (#47756), MCP subagent process leaks (#25015)
  • Claude Code: MCP server recompilation tax (#109426)
  • OpenCode: MCP opencode_console silent 403 reconnects (#59806)

4. Subagent reliability & permission propagation

  • Gemini CLI: subagent MAX_TURNS reported as success (#22323), generalist agent hangs (#21409), Browser Agent ignoring settings (#22267)
  • Copilot CLI: subagents refuse /tmp writes despite allow-all (#5441), delegated children can't auth MCP (#5437)
  • Claude Code: idle teammate stuck in Stop hook's background_tasks (#109427)
  • Codex: agent-tree suspension/recovery design (#61198)

5. Observability of agent state and tool outputs

  • OpenCode: shell exit code/elapsed time/log path exposure (#63647), stale-model footer (#63506)
  • Gemini CLI: subagent trajectories in /chat share (#22598)
  • Qwen Code: machine-readable HTTP statuses in headless errors (#16686), failed todo_write surfacing (#16679)
  • Copilot CLI: misleading auth-failure messages masking structured errors (#5436)

4. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension Claude Code Codex Gemini CLI Copilot CLI OpenCode Pi Qwen Code
Primary focus Agentic experimentation (Code Mode), desktop/cloud parity Enterprise Windows + VS Code, Rust core Subagent orchestration, AST tooling GitHub/Microsoft ecosystem, MDM fleets Plugin/API stability, V2 migration Terminal correctness, minimal footprint Unified agent loop, subscription integration
Target user Power devs, org fleet admins Windows enterprise, Rust-tooling contributors Google Cloud + Pro subscribers GitHub Enterprise, regulated orgs Plugin authors, V2 early adopters Multiplexer/headless/SSH users Qwen subscription users, CI/headless
Technical approach Tool-call → JS Code Mode (opt-in) Rust workspace (1.99.1), SPIFFE identity, seccomp Zero-dep OS sandboxing, Gemini 3 bash fluency Node CLI, ACP mode, Entra broker Multi-model "Advisor", hook metadata propagation Native TUI, XDG-compliant, provider adapters Event-driven query() kernel, experimental.unifiedAgentLoop
Contribution model Maintainer-gated (1 stale PR) Bot-merged at scale (copyberry) Maintainer-led workstreams Low PR activity High contributor churn, rapid reverts Community contributor-led (petrroll, acmerfight) Rapid release + tracking issues
Distinguishing bet Code Mode as architectural experiment Windows-first enterprise hardening Subagent self-awareness & habit Integration depth with GitHub Plugin surface stability pre-GA Silent-correction correctness 1.0 loop consolidation

Key contrasts:

  • Claude Code and Codex are the two most "enterprise-pull" tools but diverge sharply: Codex is Windows-first engineering (Computer Use, WSL, AppX), Claude Code is auth-surface-first (passkeys, WebAuthn, cross-surface parity).
  • Gemini CLI and Qwen Code both run formalized tracking-issue roadmaps (P1 kernels, unified loops), unlike the more chaotic forums of OpenCode and Pi.
  • Pi and Copilot CLI are the two with the most terminal-native focus — Pi on multiplexer/XDG correctness, Copilot on masked-dialog and screen-reader accessibility.
  • OpenCode is the only project with the Advisor dual-model pattern in-window — a genuinely distinct architectural direction versus single-model competitors.

5. Community Momentum & Maturity

Highest raw engagement (upvote/comment leaders):

  • Claude Code: #84862 passkey request at 184 👍 — highest single-item endorsement in the entire dataset, indicating a large, motivated, and organized user base.
  • OpenAI Codex: #25319 VS Code workspace scoping at 134 👍 / 60 comments — the most-discussed single issue across all tools.
  • Pi: #2870 XDG compliance at 75 👍 — a standards-compliance win with outsized community resonance.
  • Codex Discussions: 8 concurrent threads (collab workspaces, agent handoff protocols, MCP service launches) — the only tool with a thriving Discussions channel in this window, suggesting a more mature community-governance layer than competitors.

Rapid-release iterators:

  • Qwen Code — five artifacts in 24h including a 1.0 preview; iteration speed is the highest in the cohort, albeit with CI instability as the visible cost.
  • Codex — 13 merged PRs in 24h, toolchain upgrades, security fixes (seccomp x32), enterprise identity (SPIFFE).
  • Pi — large closed-PR wave led by named contributors; highest individual leverage (PR #12109 closing five issues at once).

Momentum concerns:

  • Copilot CLI — zero PRs, auth-dominated issue tracker, no Discussions activity. Momentum is entirely consumption-side; contributor pipeline appears thin or gated.
  • Claude Code — one stale PR open since July, issue-dominated tracker, and a cluster of auth regressions that are likely suppressing trust. The community is highly engaged but notably not contributing code — a signal about contribution friction.
  • Gemini CLI — no releases, maintainer-led design threads, and a recurring auth loop blocking paying Pro users (#29267). Steady but not accelerating.

Maturity ranking (colloquial):

  1. Codex — mature process, high merge throughput, enterprise-grade fixes, active Discussions
  2. Claude Code — mature product, but contribution model and auth regressions are friction points
  3. Qwen Code — fast-maturing 1.x, strong roadmap clarity, but CI debt
  4. Gemini CLI — mid-maturity, maintainer-driven, subagent reliability still forming
  5. Copilot CLI — enterprise-ready surface, but community/contributor layer underdeveloped
  6. OpenCode — industrious but pre-GA V2; correctness churn visible
  7. Pi — small but highly focused and responsive; quality-per-contributor is high

6. Trend Signals

For decision-makers evaluating tooling:

  1. Agent runtimes are now infrastructure, and infrastructure reliability is the buying criterion. Every tool's top-priority bugs are lifecycle bugs (subagent hangs, mid-task termination, resource leaks), not model-quality bugs. Budget for runtime reliability evaluation, not just token pricing.

  2. MCP auth is the new integration tax. Five of seven tools report MCP authentication pain spanning Windows (Entra), Google (OAuth), macOS (keychain), and delegated subagents. Expect to invest in MCP auth plumbing regardless of tool choice, and prioritize tools with delegated-agent auth propagation (currently weak across the board).

  3. Workspace/session scoping is a cross-tool gap, not a UX detail. Codex's most-voted issue is scoping chats to workspaces; OpenCode has hooks for it; Claude Code's cloud sessions lack image attach. Treat session-scope guarantees as a procurement requirement for multi-repo orgs.

  4. Platform coverage is uneven and quantifiably so. Windows is roughest in Codex (Computer Use, WSL, reconnect). Wayland is rough in Gemini CLI and OpenCode. Multiplexers (tmux/screen) are rough in Pi. Match tool choice to your developers' actual terminal environments — the mainstream marketing sites won't tell you this.

For developers building on these tools:

  1. Plugin/extension APIs are still settling. OpenCode's explicit "stabilize V2 plugin API pre-GA" trajectory, Claude Code's new engines["claude-code"] constraint, and Pi's request for lightweight extension subpath exports (#11446) all indicate the extension layer is in flux. Pin to specific versions and budget for migration.

  2. Structured tool output is becoming a first-class contract. OpenCode (#63647), Qwen Code (#16686), and Codex (#61222 trace schema v3) are all formalizing tool outputs (exit codes, status, payload schemas). Write for the machine-readable form, not the human string.

  3. Dual-model and multi-model reasoning is arriving. OpenCode's Advisor tool (#63637) — where the active model consults a secondary model — is the clearest signal yet that the next architectural frontier is composable reasoning, not just bigger single models. Watch this pattern; if it ships and sticks, competitors will follow.

  4. Subscription/usage-limit thinking is shifting from "metering" to "degradation contracts." Codex (#60447), Qwen Code (#17038), and OpenCode (#63568 opaque quota) all surface the same emerging user expectation: a session that hits a limit should degrade gracefully, not die mid-task. Tools that implement checkpoint-then-suspend will win trust in long-horizon work.

  5. Primary-source signal > marketing. The 184-👍 passkey request, 134-👍 VS Code scoping, and 75-👍 XDG compliance tell you what users actually need more reliably than any roadmap blog. Monitor issue upvote velocity as a leading indicator of the next feature each vendor ships.

Report compiled from 2026-11-13 community digests across seven AI CLI projects. Upvote and comment counts reflect the snapshot at generation time and may have moved.

Per-Tool Reports

Claude Code — anthropics/claude-code

Claude Code Skills Highlights

Source: anthropics/skills

Claude Code Skills — Community Highlights Report

Data snapshot: 2026-11-13 · Source: github.com/anthropics/skills

1. Top Skills Ranking (Most-Discussed PRs)

Note: the PR dataset lists Comments: undefined for all entries, so ranking below is inferred from cross-referenced issue activity, update frequency, and thematic prominence.

# Skill / PR Functionality Discussion Highlights Status
1 mcp-builder fix (#1742) Updates MCP connection scripts for mcp>=2.0.0 (streamable_http_client rename, custom headers via create_mcp_http_client) Fixes #1668; breaking API change in MCP SDK affecting all MCP-based skills OPEN

Also notable: document-typography (#514), scnet-hpc (#1615), and a cluster of skill-creator correctness fixes (#1681, #1997).

2. Community Demand Trends (from Issues)

  • Trust & namespace security — Issue #492 (46 comments) is the single most-discussed issue: community skills shipping under the anthropic/ namespace create a trust-boundary abuse risk.
  • Org-wide skill sharing — Issue #228 (17 comments, 8 👍) requests a shared skill library / direct share links instead of manual .skill file exchange.
  • Eval/trigger reliability — Issues #556 (13 comments) and #1352 (6 comments) report that run_eval.py yields 0% or false-negative trigger rates — a systemic quality problem for skill authors.
  • Context-window economics — Issue #1487: claude-api skill eagerly injects ~156k tokens in one tool call.
  • Plugin duplication — Issue #189 (9 👍): document-skills and example-skills install identical content.
  • Governance & quality pipelines — Issues #412 (agent-governance) and #1385 (Reasoning Quality Gate Pipeline) signal demand for safety/verification-oriented skills.
  • Persistent memory — Issue #1329 proposes compact-memory (symbolic notation for agent state).

Emerging directions: workflow automation (spec→tasks), document QA (typography, orphaned comments), security/governance, media generation, and eval tooling.

3. High-Potential Pending Skills

These active PRs (recently updated, still OPEN) are the most likely to land soon:

  • mcp-builder MCP v2 compatibility — #1742 · updated 2026-10-08
  • notion-spec-to-implementation + quantitative-resume-auditor — #1245 · updated 2026-10-15
  • webapp-testing shell=True removal — #1980 · updated 2026-11-01
  • docx LibreOffice timeout fix — #1792 · updated 2026-11-01
  • xlsx external-links resolution — #2019 · updated 2026-11-03
  • claude-api docs sync (pause_turn) — #1950 · updated 2026-11-10
  • pyxel retro game skill — #525 · updated 2026-11-01 (long-running but persistent)

4. Skills Ecosystem Insight

The community's most concentrated demand is not for new capabilities but for reliability, security, and trust infrastructure around existing skills — fixing eval/trigger correctness, hardening scripts against injection and context blow-up, and resolving namespace/identity ambiguity so users can safely delegate to community-authored skills.

Claude Code Community Digest — 2026-11-13

1. Today's Highlights

Anthropic shipped v2.1.323, introducing experimental Code Mode (Claude writes JavaScript to call its own tools) and a new engines["claude-code"] constraint field for plugin compatibility. Community attention is split between a highly-upvoted passkey/WebAuthn authentication request (184 👍) and a cluster of auth-related regressions — forced mid-session re-login killing background subagents, Android Play Integrity sign-in failures, and a help-form redirect loop. A steady stream of sandbox, hooks, and MCP bugs continues to dominate fresh issue filings.

2. Releases

v2.1.323

  • Code Mode (experimental, opt-in): Claude writes JavaScript to invoke its tools instead of using the standard tool-call path. Can be enabled/disabled per-organization via the docs at code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode. This is a notable architectural experiment worth watching for agentic workflows.
  • Plugin engine constraints: plugin.json now supports engines["claude-code"], allowing plugins to declare a required Claude Code version; plugins outside their stated range are now handled (rejected/flagged).

3. Hot Issues

# Issue Why it matters Reaction
#84862 Passkey (WebAuthn) sign-in across every surface The single most-upvoted open request; users want passwordless auth everywhere Claude is available. 37 comments, 184 👍
#105770 Android sign-in fails with Play Integrity "unverified" (HTTP 400 on /auth/verify_google_mobile) Blocks rooted/unlocked-bootloader users entirely — a growing, legitimate developer segment. 13 comments, 10 👍

#109427 Idle teammate remains in Stop hook's background_tasks forever Hook authors receive stale agent state, complicating orchestration logic. New today

Also notable: #106049 (cloud sessions can't attach images to PRs — GitHub proxy rejects all GraphQL), #108577 (expose voice dictation to Agent SDK), #109414 (claude stop --all bulk command).

4. Key PR Progress

Only one PR was updated in the last 24h:

#81672 fix(hookify) — make package import independent of install directory name. 6. Feature Request Trends

Distilling across all issues and PRs in this window, the dominant directions are:

  • Provider/transport flexibility — non-streaming mode (#785), Responses API for the Go service (#23655), Bedrock inference-profile correctness (#53756), GitLab Duo tool-calling repair (#63212), and "unload local model on /clear and /exit " (#63612). Users want broader, more reliable backend coverage.
  • Headless/enterprise readiness — MSI installer and silent deploy switches (#48099), permission-request timeouts (#61504), and GitHub OAuth/commit attribution (#54670). Requests cluster around managed, unattended environments.
  • Multi-model reasoning workflows — the advisor tool (#63631/#63637) is the clearest new direction: let the active model consult a second model.
  • TUI/UX parity with V1 — timestamps (#49742), RTL support (#26915), collapsible compaction summaries (#48596), and stale-model footer display (#63506) are all about restoring or extending terminal UX.
  • Plugin/API surface stability — V2 model-context hook (#35408), per-session tool availability (#35647), durable naming review (#34922), and metadata hook fixes (#63252/#63590) point to plugin authors needing a stable, documented V2 API before GA.

7. Developer Pain Points

Recurring frustrations across the dataset:

  • V2 regressions eroding trust: missing timestamps (#49742), stale model in footer (#63506), and silent turn aborts (#63632) each describe the UI/engine showing something different from reality. The #63632 author explicitly notes the tracker asked for this report "twice" — friction with triage.
  • Silent failures and swallowed errors: tool-name collision from normalization (#52420), MCP opencode_console 403 with silent 6-second reconnects (#59806), and GitLab Duo turns ending "with no output and no error" (#63212). Errors aren't surfaced to users.
  • Performance/scale issues: git polling saturating CPU on 1.3M-file worktrees (#62948), long agent turns dying mid-stream with ECONNRESET (#60940), and even one-word prompts taking a very long time on Desktop 2.2.7 (#63576).
  • Install/upgrade friction: raw npm EACCES stack traces on root-owned global prefixes, with an older v1 binary potentially shadowing the new one on PATH (#63626).
  • Platform-specific gaps: Wayland clipboard image paste does nothing on GNOME (#63567); Desktop renderer crashes on Windows x64 (#63001).
  • Free-tier rate limiting confusion: #63568 reports a hit limit after a four-week idle period despite near-zero usage — opaque quota accounting.

The through-line: the community is heavily invested in V2 but is hitting correctness, observability, and platform-ergonomics rough edges. The rapid back-and-forth on tool-repair PRs (#63630 revert → #63633 → #63573) suggests the maintainers are themselves iterating quickly under contributor pressure.

Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-11-13

1. Today's Highlights

A large batch of long-standing issues and PRs were closed on 2026-11-12, spanning terminal-rendering correctness, provider integrations (Copilot reasoning effort, Google custom fetch, Qwen Token Plan branding), and crash-class bugs in the read/bash tools. The dominant theme is a coordinated cleanup of "TUI writes to the terminal behind its own back" problems, led by contributor petrroll, alongside several high-priority reliability fixes from acmerfight. Community demand remains strongest for stability under constrained environments (read-only FS, full /tmp, slow clients, nested terminals like tmux/screen).

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #2870 [CLOSED] Follow XDG Base Directory — 28 comments, 75 👍. The single highest-signal item in the digest: Pi was cluttering $HOME with config/state dirs on Linux instead of honoring $XDG_CONFIG_HOME. Its closure marks a meaningful standards-compliance win and explains the unusually high upvote count (75). Why it matters: filesystem-convention bugs are quietly corrosive for Linux power users and dotfile managers (Nix, home-manager, chezmoi).

  2. #10628 [OPEN] OSC 52 copy in fullscreen TUI swallowed by tmux — 14 comments. Copy-on-select emits a raw OSC 52 escape sequence that tmux intercepts into its own paste buffer instead of relaying. Pi falsely reports "Copied!" either way — a dangerous silent-failure mode on headless SSH hosts where there is no LOCAL clipboard fallback. Why it matters: clipboard correctness is a trust issue for remote workflows; users only discover the failure downstream.

  3. #12019 [OPEN] [prio:p0] github-copilot: Gemini models never get reasoning_effort — 9 comments. The bundled Copilot catalog hardcodes supportsReasoningEffort: false for all openai-completions models, so --thinking is silently a no-op on Gemini models and usage.reasoning_tokens is ignored. Why it matters: a P0 that silently disables a flagship feature; a fix PR (#12110) is already open.

  4. #11026 [OPEN] [durable] permanently delete a conversation — 8 comments, 6 👍. Requests harness.deleteConversation(id, ctx) that refuses while a run is active, then removes entries, docs, inbox items, and scheduler state. Why it matters: data-lifecycle completeness in pi-durable; users currently have no first-class deletion path.

  5. #10618 [OPEN] GNU screen: inherited COLORTERM overrides screen guard — 7 comments. screen passes COLORTERM=truecolor through, but its own truecolor option is off by default, so the TUI emits 24-bit color that gets mangled and colors vanish. Why it matters: same family as the tmux bug — multiplexer environment detection is a recurring blind spot.

  6. #10563 [CLOSED] MCP OAuth: Google servers never get a refresh token — 6 comments. Google only issues refresh tokens when access_type=offline is sent; the ability to add authorization-request parameters now makes Gmail/Calendar MCP servers usable long-term. Why it matters: unblocks persistent OAuth for Google's MCP surface.

  7. #8617 [OPEN] Codex: use file references for image-heavy tool results — 6 comments. Proposes storing image bytes locally and materializing outbound images as ChatGPT file_id references instead of replaying base64 on every request. The author has a working prototype. Why it matters: a direct payload-size and cost lever for image-heavy agent workflows.

  8. #10585 [OPEN] [prio:p0] bash temp-file stream errors crash the whole process — 4 comments. On 1.0.4, an ENOSPC on /tmp (or EACCES) produced an uncaught exception that killed the process mid-run, with the in-flight run lost and no tool error surfaced. Why it matters: a crash in constrained environments; exactly the class of bug that erodes trust in unattended runs.

  9. #9448 [OPEN] pi auth check cannot see extension-registered providers — 4 comments. The documented scriptable readiness check reports extension providers as invalid_state, breaking non-interactive pipelines that gate on it. Why it matters: small-looking inconsistency with outsized impact on CI/review automation.

  10. #11446 [OPEN] [durable] lightweight extension-authoring entry point — 2 comments. Requests a @earendil-works/pi-durable/extension subpath exporting defineDoc, defineExtension, hook, and ToolTask without pulling in session runtime, storage, or model code. Why it matters: extension authors currently pay a heavy import cost for pure type/helper usage.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #12116 [CLOSED] fix(coding-agent): anchor find path patterns at the search path — Fixes #12066. find src/**/*.ts was matching files above the project root because fd --full-path globs against absolute paths. Impact: eliminates cross-project false positives in a core tool.

  2. #12110 [OPEN] fix(ai): send reasoning_effort and read reasoning tokens for GitHub Copilot — Closes the P0 #12019; sources supportsReasoningEffort from models.dev and additionally enables it for gemini-4-carbon. Impact: restores --thinking semantics on Copilot.

  3. #12109 [CLOSED] fix(tui): hide terminal images covered by overlays — Closes #11584 and duplicates #6995, #9439, #10863, #11284. compositeTuiLine passed image rows through, leaving a "hole" in overlays. Impact: one fix retiring five issues — the highest-leverage TUI PR in this batch.

  4. #12112 [CLOSED] fix(ai): move Qwen Token Plan to current gateways and model lists — Closes #11773, covers remaining model-list problems from #7491/#7674; defaults all four Qwen Token Plan providers to current hosts. Impact: prevents auth/routing failures against deprecated endpoints.

  5. #12111 [CLOSED] fix(coding-agent): keep /resume selection stable during progressive reload — After delete/rename, a partially loaded list clamps the index onto an unrelated session. Impact: fixes a subtly destructive UX bug during session cleanup.

  6. #12107 [CLOSED] fix(extensions): bound session_shutdown dispatch so quit cannot hang — Quitting sometimes left pi running for days after the TUI disappeared (observed on macOS with gentle-shell). Impact: fixes a zombie-process class bug that is very hard for users to diagnose.

  7. #11966 [CLOSED] fix(coding-agent): stop writing to the terminal while the TUI draws — Fixes #11264. Direct stdout/stderr writes left the TUI's screen model stale, causing persistent redraw artifacts. Impact: architectural hygiene; several follow-ups (#12117, #12115, #11973) continue the sweep.

  8. #11952 [CLOSED] fix(coding-agent): run bash calls alone, other calls in parallel — Closes #11950. Prevents a read from racing a concurrent bash that is supposed to produce the file. Impact: removes a real correctness hazard in mixed tool batches.

  9. #12087 [CLOSED] fix(coding-agent): skip VCS directories in grep and find — Closes #12084. --hidden was causing .git/ internals (reflogs, hook samples) to pollute results — 15 of 18 TODO matches in the report were from .git/. Impact: noise reduction in the two most-used search tools.

  10. #12093 [CLOSED] fix(ai): retry provider errors reading "Connection closed." — Adds the common mid-stream gateway drop to isRetryableAssistantError. Impact: converts a hard turn failure into a transparent retry.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this period.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Data lifecycle & persistence controls: explicit deletion for pi-durable conversations (#11026), extension-authoring subpath exports (#11446) — the durable layer is maturing from "works" toward "manageable."
  • Terminal/environment correctness: XDG compliance (#2870), tmux OSC 52 passthrough (#10628), GNU screen truecolor handling (#10618) — a consistent push for Pi to behave well in multiplexers and standards-compliant Linux environments.
  • Provider fidelity: reasoning effort propagation for Copilot/Gemini (#12019), custom fetch in Google adapters (#12097), MCP OAuth authorization parameters for Google (#10563), namespace-scoped tool_search (#11558).
  • Payload efficiency: file-reference-based image handling for Codex (#8617), prompt-cache-preserving branch summaries (#9411).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Silent failures: Pi reports "Copied!" when tmux swallowed the copy (#10628); settings changes look successful on a read-only settings.json with no error (#10168); --thinking is accepted but silently ignored on Copilot models (#12019). Users cannot distinguish success from a no-op.
  • Crash-instead-of-degrade: uncaught ENOSPC/EACCES on bash temp files (#10585), uncaught AbortError on aborted reads (#12118), and pi.exec mapping signal-killed commands to exit code 0 (#12089) — resource exhaustion and signals turn into lost runs or false success.
  • Multi-tenant terminal environments: tmux, GNU screen, and nested SSH sessions repeatedly break clipboard and color behavior, suggesting environment detection logic needs a consolidated pass rather than per-multiplexer patches.
  • Tooling noise: VCS directories polluting grep/find (#12087), path globs escaping the search root (#12066) — small annoyances that compound across long agent sessions.

Note: counts reflect the data snapshot as presented; several issues were updated on 2026-11-12/13 and may have closed since.

Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-11-13

1. Today's Highlights

The 1.0 preview line took center stage today with the release of v1.0.0-preview.1, which fixes Qwen subscription account sign-in and syncs the subscription model catalog/thinking-budget mapping. In parallel, the team continued hardening the v0.27.3 release across CLI, SDK (TypeScript v0.1.33), and Desktop, while a major tracking issue (#17045) opened to land the 1.0 event-driven loop kernel on main incrementally. CI stability remains the dominant operational theme, with multiple flaky-test and infrastructure issues (inode exhaustion, artifact timeouts) under active triage.

2. Releases

  • v0.27.3 — Stable release of the CLI. Release notes are currently a stub (qwen-release-notes:v1), with the full change list to follow.
  • sdk-typescript-v0.1.33 — Bundles CLI 0.27.3 (built from the same branch/ref as the SDK). Note: the release body also references CLI 0.27.2, suggesting a possible note-generation merge artifact worth watching.
  • desktop-v0.27.3 — Desktop build. Includes CI prettier-ignore fixes (#16729) and Agent Host retrieval fixes.
  • v1.0.0-preview.1 — Preview release. Headline fix: subscription accounts can now use subscription models after sign-in, with the model catalog following sign-in state automatically (no manual provider config). Subscription catalog and thinking-budget mapping synced with Qwen Code 0.2x.
  • v0.27.2-nightly.20261112 — Nightly with managed-agent fixes: releasing the MCP owner when a Session closes (#16728) and hardening the managed-agent host.

Feature note: A new UI affordance added chips above the Web Shell composer for unfinished background workflows, shells, monitors, and local agents.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #17045 — tracking(core): land the 1.0 Preview loop kernel on main (P1, 7 comments) — The central roadmap issue for migrating the event-driven query() kernel from v1.0.0-preview to main, one surface at a time with a switch back. High strategic importance for anyone building on the agent loop.
  2. #15327 — tracking(core): run every surface on one agent loop behind experimental.unifiedAgentLoop (P1) — Companion tracking issue to #17045. Signals a consolidation of the loop implementation across all surfaces; critical for long-term API stability.
  3. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate (342 comments) — The longest-running CI failure thread on the tracker. Enormous comment volume reflects sustained automation churn rather than new user impact, but it's a persistent maintenance tax.
  4. #16927 — CI built-tree download timeouts redden PR checks with no tests run (P1, 7 comments) — All 58 jobs on the hz fleet affected; artifact handoff expires on both attempts, turning PRs red after ~31 minutes without executing a single test. Directly blocks contributor velocity.
  5. #17040 — ACP session child goes idle-unresponsive after curl/network calls (P1, 5 comments) — Web Shell sessions die with agent channel closed mid-request when a turn runs curl through a local proxy; the child isn't crashing but stops answering the daemon. Real user-facing reliability bug in the daemon path.
  6. #13570 — Auto mode blocks inert text mentioning the amend phrase (P2, 9 comments) — A permissions false-positive: the destructive-command guard fires on text that merely mentions the amend phrase, ahead of the user's own ask rule, with no escape hatch. Security/UX tension worth resolving.
  7. #16579 — Hosted v1 detach wedges on a Hook-configured turn's live background run (P1, 4 comments) — Scope was corrected on 2026-11-12: the wedge is on the v1 detach path, needs a keep-READY drain. Important for managed/hosted deployments.
  8. #17038 — CLI stuck in login verification state on headless Linux (P2, 3 comments) — OAuth flow over headless Linux with browser-on-another-machine doesn't auto-continue. Common CI/SSH developer scenario.
  9. #16915 — Task reports "connection to the model service was interrupted" and cannot continue (P2, closed) — User-reported task interruption; closed quickly. Mirrors recurring connection-loss complaints (see also #16908).
  10. #16449 — core(permissions): extend amend-guard inert proof and recognizer coverage (P2, 5 comments) — Follow-up to #16075. Tracks the remaining non-blocking security-hardening items from review, keeping a fail-closed backstop.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #17055 — feat(core): resolve loop switches per surface with env force on/off — Lets each surface resolve its own experimental loop switch, with environment override. Foundational for the #17045 rollout.
  2. #17050 — feat(ci): add kernel and OpenTUI nightly legs for the loop rollout — Adds the nightly E2E legs the loop rollout depends on, including a third kernel arm for the Linux sandbox:none matrix and three-arm loop matrix for OpenTUI.
  3. #16528 — feat(web-shell): resume an interrupted turn when a session loads — Automatically resumes persisted turns interrupted by daemon/environment restarts instead of leaving them idle behind Continue. Meaningful reliability win for Web Shell.
  4. #17088 — feat(managed-agent): fixed-interval /loop schedules for Managed Sessions — Enables recurring /loop schedules in Managed Sessions, leveraging H6 definitions, single-claim scanner, and run ledger. Expands automation capability.
  5. #16661 — fix(mcp): repair the MCP connection torn down by an aborted tool call — Aborting an in-flight MCP request could leave a dead transport; the abort path now repairs the connection. Fixes a real session-degradation bug.
  6. #16686 — feat(headless): keep provider HTTP status on terminal error results — Terminal error envelopes now carry an optional status (401/429/5xx) for machine-readable consumers. Valuable for CI/headless integrations.
  7. #16679 — fix(acp): surface failed todo_write calls instead of dropping them — Failed todo writes now emit a terminal tool_call_update with status: failed rather than silently producing no frame. Better observability for ACP clients.
  8. #17012 — feat(channels): add Feishu custom bot webhook delivery — Adds a send-only Feishu custom-bot Channel with Markdown card delivery for Notify, prompt results, and scheduled results. Expands integrations.
  9. #16779 — feat(web-shell): improve session search experience — Dedicated centered dialog, clear titles/snippets/workspace context, keyboard selection, focus restoration, loading/retry states.
  10. #16924 — fix(core): let glob match directories, not just files — Previously every real directory was filtered out while a symlink pointing at one survived, producing inconsistent existence probes. Correctness fix.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussion data was provided in the source. This section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Unified agent loop / session management — The strongest emerging direction. Two P1 tracking issues (#17045, #15327) target landing a single event-driven loop kernel across all surfaces, gated experimentally. This is the defining 1.x roadmap bet.
  • Background & scheduled workflow visibility — New composer chips for unfinished background workflows/shells/monitors/local agents, plus recurring /loop schedules in Managed Sessions (#17088), point to growing demand for long-running, asynchronous task management.
  • Integration channels — Feishu bot webhook delivery (#17012) signals appetite for broader notification/delivery integrations beyond the existing surfaces.
  • Headless/CI ergonomics — Machine-readable error statuses (#16686) and headless OAuth fixes (#17038) reflect real demand for scriptable, automation-friendly behavior.
  • Web Shell polish — Session search redesign (#16779), interrupted-turn resume (#16528), and focus fixes (#17089) indicate active investment in the Web Shell UX.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. CI instability is the top friction — Multiple P1 CI issues (#16927, #17037, #14724, #11680) describe PRs going red with no tests run (artifact download timeouts), /tmp inode exhaustion on hz3 hosts, and long-running managed-agent gate failures. This is directly blocking contributor throughput and consuming maintainer bandwidth.
  2. Connection reliability / silent interruption — Recurring reports (#16915, #16908, #17040, #17038) of model connection losses, stuck sessions, and daemon-killed ACP children mid-request. Users repeatedly lack detailed logs to diagnose root causes.
  3. Permission-guard false positives — The auto-mode guard firing on inert text that merely mentions the amend phrase (#13570), with no escape hatch and taking precedence over the user's own instruction, is a notable security-vs-usability tension.
  4. Flaky test noise — A high volume of auto-filed deflake: issues (#17063, #17057, #17046, #17079, #17084, #16975) from the CI Failure Patrol indicates persistent nondeterminism in Web Shell E2E and process-bootstrap tests.
  5. Dependency security debt — #16434 tracks published advisories still resolved by @qwen-code/sdk@0.1.28 and @qwen-code/web-shell@0.26.8, awaiting dependency upgrades and republishing.
  6. Windows/daemon edge cases — #17040 (Windows ACP child idle-unresponsive after curl) and #13570 (macOS/VS Code permissions) reflect platform-specific gaps in the daemon and permissions paths.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-13

Issues: 432 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-13 01:46 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-13

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains a high-velocity, high-complexity project with 432 issues and 500 PRs updated in the last 24 hours (263 active issues, 284 open PRs), indicating sustained contributor engagement but also a growing maintenance load. No new releases shipped today, and the project is currently operating without a stable release containing several in-flight fixes; multiple issues reference fixes that exist only in prereleases (v2026.11.5-beta.1/.2) and not in stable. The issue tracker is dominated by state-management, session-recovery, and SQLite/WAL problems, suggesting the persistence layer is the primary source of instability. Activity is healthy but the ratio of open-to-closed issues and the volume of clawsweeper:needs-maintainer-review tags point to a maintainer review bottleneck as the key risk to project health.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. There are no release notes, breaking changes, or migration guidance to report today.

Notable context from issues: several fixes are staged in prereleases but not yet in stable:

  • Issue #141474 notes the historical-state recovery fix ships only in v2026.11.5-beta.1 and v2026.11.5-beta.2, not in stable v2026.11.3, v2026.11.2, or v2026.9.37.

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed PRs today: 216 (merged or closed). Highlights from the PR list:

  • #197887 [CLOSED] — perf(agents): reuse sealed nested tool-result payloads — reduces normalization work when persisting already-sealed Tool Search results. (link)
  • #196812 [CLOSED] — fix(sessions): confirmed deliveries record a false delivery-failed when media cannot be embedded — corrects misleading delivery status in transcripts. (link)
  • #197983 [CLOSED] — fix(ui): desktop group search misses accented group names typed in another Unicode form — Unicode normalization (NFC/NFD) fix for group search. (link)

Open PRs advancing features (awaiting review):

  • #196200 [OPEN] — Agent GitHub account management in Profile UI (Closes #196136). (link)
  • #197904 [OPEN] — Open Chrome settings pages from Control UI Browser panel. (link)
  • #197814 [OPEN] — New CLI commands openclaw agents files list/get. (link)
  • #197990 [OPEN] — fix(agents): plugin agent_end hooks fail after a turn that called dispatch_action (P1, has regression test). (link)

4. Community Hot Topics

Most active issues by comment count:

Issue Comments Theme Link
#164294 40 Gateway WAL auto-checkpoint never completes (blocked by in-process reader) link
#191944 27 macOS gateway stop/stop --force fail with "Process ancestry could not be fully inspected" link
#120385 26 Code Mode tool catalog incomplete for cron/memory-flush turns link
#67413 17 Per-agent dreaming configuration (memory spikes/OOM) — CLOSED link
#44309 17 One-way A2A dispatch mode (no reply-back ping-pong) — CLOSED link

Underlying needs analysis:

  • The top issues cluster around operational reliability under scale: WAL checkpointing, process lifecycle on macOS, and SQLite contention. Users running long-lived gateways with large databases are hitting structural limits, not one-off bugs.
  • The A2A/dispatch and per-agent dreaming requests (both closed) reflect demand for finer-grained multi-agent orchestration control — operators want to prevent runaway resource use and unwanted message loops.

Hot PRs: Several P2 performance PRs from steipete (#198008, #198028, #198027) target moving work off the Gateway main thread — a recurring, high-impact theme.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

P0 / Release-Blocker

  • #190563 [OPEN, P0] — Regression: Cannot resume paused Codex chat; provider review/native thread mismatch. Tagged impact:ux-release-blocker. No fix PR linked. (link)

P1 (High Severity)

  • #144291 [OPEN, P1] — Config hot-reload aborts every in-flight agent turn ("prepared model runtime plugin generation was superseded"). Message loss. Needs security review. (link)
  • #144809 [OPEN, P1] — claude-cli: turns longer than RUN_STALE_TAKEOVER_MS lose their entire generated reply. (link)
  • #191841 [OPEN, P1] — 2026.10.10 regression: 'native child reaping is unavailable' breaks all exec on Linux with glibc < 2.31 (RHEL 8/al8). (link)
  • #196199 [OPEN, P1] — Regression since 2026.10.10: native Codex helper completions fail to resume parent, locking users out. (link)
  • #181459 [OPEN, P1] — 3.5 GB agent DB makes startup a gamble; agent UNAVAILABLE with 'commit checkpoint expired'. (link)
  • #168101 [CLOSED, P1] — Rate-limit Retry-After ignores maxRetryDelayMs after a tool call. (link)

P2 (Notable)

  • #162585 [OPEN] — Windows plugin source-capture staging never converges; 290 MB → 612 MB+ growth. (link)
  • #101929 [OPEN] — Context-overflow estimator over-counts 2.3–2.6x vs billed usage. (link)
  • #197374 [OPEN] — Compaction silently degrades on long sessions (120s idle timeout caps budget). (link)

Fix PRs exist for: #197990 (agent_end hooks, P1), #196812 (delivery-failed, merged/closed), #197510 (session path checks off Gateway thread).

Stability pattern: Recurring regressions tied to the 2026.10.10 release (#191841, #196199) and SQLite/WAL/checkpoint subsystem (#164294, #181459, #197083) are the dominant risks.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Request Signal Link
Explicitly authorize cross-provider cron fallback accounts CLOSED today; likely candidate for near-term scheduling work link
Limit-aware model fallback (skip exhausted provider accounts) CLOSED; aligns with rate-limit fixes link
Doctor recovery for stranded requester settle wake Open, operator-recovery focus link
Feishu (Lark) progress streaming mode Open; parity with Slack/Discord/Telegram link
Per-agent compaction/contextPruning overrides in agents.list CLOSED; strong multi-agent customization signal link
Accessibility: chat messages as headings for screen readers Open link
Plugin hook to append content after tool results in-flight Open; plugin extensibility gap link

Prediction: The next minor release is likely to emphasize (a) provider fallback/rate-limit intelligence (multiple closed requests converge here), (b) multi-agent configuration granularity (per-agent compaction, dreaming), and (c) Gateway-thread performance work (many open steipete PRs).

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points:

  • Startup unreliability at scale — large agent DBs (3.5 GB) make startup a "gamble" (#181459); agents go UNAVAILABLE with checkpoint-expired errors.
  • Silent failures and message loss — replies discarded after long turns (#144809), hot-reload aborting turns (#144291), and false delivery-failed records (#196812).
  • Platform-specific breakage — macOS process ancestry inspection (#191944), Windows plugin staging (#162585), RHEL 8/glibc exec regression (#191841).
  • Version confusion — fixes exist in prereleases but not stable; users on stable are stranded (#141474, #48920 "Live Docs ahead of release").

Satisfaction signals: Users are investing significant effort filing detailed, well-instrumented reports (many with source-pinned repros and live-Gateway tests), indicating high engagement and goodwill. However, the volume of needs-maintainer-review and needs-product-decision tags suggests growing frustration with review latency.

8. Backlog Watch

Important items needing maintainer attention (stale and/or high-impact):

Issue/PR Status Why it matters Link
#164294 Open since 2026-10-03, 40 comments, needs-maintainer-review Gateway WAL checkpoint never completes — core reliability link
#120385 Open since 2026-08-08, needs-info Code Mode tool catalog incomplete for cron turns link
#114067 Open since 2026-07-26, queueable-fix, fix-shape-clear --help 35x slower with plugins key — clear, fixable perf win link
#180978 Open since 2026-10-22, needs-product-decision Active Memory circuit breaker never opens at chat pace link
#170562 Open, needs-product-decision Doctor recovery for stranded requester settle wake link
#154524 Open, needs-product-decision Screen-reader accessibility for chat navigation link

Backlog risk assessment: #164294 (40 comments, no fix PR) and #114067 (clear, low-risk perf fix) are the highest-value items currently stalled. The concentration of clawsweeper:needs-maintainer-review across the top-commented issues indicates the project would benefit from expanding maintainer review capacity or delegating triage for P2 issues.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report: Personal AI Assistant / Agent Open-Source Ecosystem

Date: 2026-11-13 | Sources: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw community digests

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent open-source landscape on 2026-11-13 is characterized by high-velocity development concentrated in a handful of large projects, with four of five surveyed projects showing 50–500+ daily issue/PR updates and only one (IronClaw) dormant. The dominant theme across the ecosystem is the painful transition from single-user tooling to multi-tenant, production-grade infrastructure: projects are simultaneously wrestling with persistence-layer reliability (SQLite/WAL, checkpoint recovery), identity and access control (OIDC, RBAC, sandboxing), and loop-correctness guardrails that fire on legitimate long-horizon agent behavior. A second converging theme is silent failure — Slack status indicators, delivery pipelines, session search, and token accounting — which erodes user trust more than crashes. Despite shared technical concerns, the projects are diverging in maturity and scope: OpenClaw operates at reference-implementation scale (~930 daily items), while Hermes, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw hover at comparable but smaller velocities (~50 items each), each carving out distinct niches (Nous research agents, AgentScope ecosystem, security-first multi-tenancy).

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers:

  • Scale of operations: OpenClaw processes ~9× Hermes's or ZeroClaw's daily item volume (930 vs. ~100). It is the de facto reference implementation, and its issue tracker functions as an industry-wide bug corpus other projects implicitly learn from.
  • Breadth of integrations and platform coverage: Issues span macOS process ancestry, Windows plugin staging, RHEL/glibc exec, Unicode search normalization — indicating a genuinely cross-platform user base that smaller projects (ZeroClaw's Windows gap, QwenPaw's Windows path bugs) have not yet matched.
  • Established tactical playbook: The clawsweeper:* tag taxonomy, P0–P2 severity discipline, and prerelease-beta staging (v2026.11.5-beta.1/.2) reflect a mature release-engineering process — albeit one currently bottlenecked.

Technical approach differences:

  • OpenClaw is the most Gateway-centric architecture, and its hottest pain points (WAL auto-checkpoint, main-thread contention, SQLite checkpoint expiry on 3.5 GB DBs) are consequences of that architectural choice at scale. Peers have not yet been stress-tested to the same degree — their equivalent bugs are latent, not surfaced.
  • The heavy concentration of steipete-authored "move work off the Gateway main thread" PRs signals the project is in an active performance-refactor phase, whereas ZeroClaw is in an identity/security phase and QwenPaw is in a plugin-migration phase.

Community size comparison:

  • OpenClaw's top issue (#164294, WAL checkpoint) has 40 comments — comparable to Hermes's #131859 (59) and ZeroClaw's #6996 (29), meaning top-thread engagement is surprisingly similar despite the 9× overall volume gap. This suggests OpenClaw's community is broader but not proportionally deeper per-thread — consistent with a large user base whose reports are triaged faster and thus generate fewer comments per item.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Activity tiers:

  • Tier 1 — Hyper-scale, review-bound: OpenClaw (930 daily items). Rapidly iterating but maintainer-review bottleneck is the binding constraint (needs-maintainer-review concentration, P0 #190563 with no fix PR, 40-comment WAL issue stalled). Momentum is sustained but throttled.
  • Tier 2 — Actively iterating, throughput-limited: Hermes, ZeroClaw, QwenPaw (~50 items each). All three show healthy intake with unhealthy closing rates (merge ratios 0.06–0.24). Each is in a distinct phase:
    • Hermes: stabilizing around v0.23.0; heavy security investment but a 2-month-old top bug (#110374) signals prioritization mismatch.
    • ZeroClaw: mid-release-launch; v0.9.0 shipped today with S0 delegation bypass (#8279) unfixed and blocking CI (#12320) red — highest risk of the tier, though also the most strategically ambitious.
    • QwenPaw: post-2.3.0 regression stabilization; distinctive strength is a responsive first-time-contributor funnel (issues reported and fix PRs opened same-day, e.g., #8700 → #8701), suggesting good mentorship/scoping.
  • Tier 3 — Dormant: IronClaw (zero activity). Should be monitored for revival or deprecation.

Maturity assessment: No project in this set is yet "stable" in the production sense. OpenClaw is the most process-mature; ZeroClaw is the most architecturally deliberate (RFC-driven, error-code taxonomy); QwenPaw is the most contributor-friendly; Hermes is the most security-invested. The ecosystem as a whole is in a "scaling adolescence" — tools that work impressively in demos break at 3.5 GB DBs, multi-workspace setups, and external-contributor onboarding.

7. Trend Signals

The following signals, extracted from cross-project community feedback, carry direct value for AI-agent developers and decision-makers:

  1. "Silent success" is the new "crash." Every project has at least one high-engagement bug where the system appears to succeed but silently drops content, status, or billing data (OpenClaw #144809, Hermes #110374/#154612, QwenPaw #8580, ZeroClaw #12405). Design implication: build first-class delivery/acknowledgement telemetry into agent loops; never infer success from absence of errors.

  2. Guardrails must distinguish "stuck" from "waiting." The QwenPaw doom-loop gate and OpenClaw memory circuit-breaker both misfire on legitimate background/polling work. Design implication: loop-control primitives need an explicit "external-wait" state, not just iteration/error counters.

  3. Multi-tenancy is the 2026-Q4 forcing function. OIDC, per-sender RBAC, per-workspace channel isolation, and delegation permission ceilings appear independently in ZeroClaw, QwenPaw, and OpenClaw. Design implication: choose your identity/isolation model before you need it; retrofitting tenancy onto single-operator assumptions is expensive.

  4. Delegation is a privilege-escalation surface. ZeroClaw's S0 (#8279, sub-agent inherits unfiltered parent tools) is an early warning the entire ecosystem will eventually face. Design implication: permission intersection (never union) across agent delegation is a baseline safety property.

  5. Billing-grade metering is a first-class feature, not a nice-to-have. Hermes's four competing usage-accounting PRs and QwenPaw's cron-usage omission show that cost visibility is now a primary user expectation. Design implication: persist model identity, cache/reasoning usage, and provider attribution on every turn.

  6. Contributor onboarding is a stability signal. Hermes's broken fork-PR path and ZeroClaw's red CI gate both block external contribution. Design implication: the health of your contribution pipeline predicts your ability to absorb the next growth phase.

  7. Review capacity — not contributor interest — is the ecosystem bottleneck. Merge-to-intake ratios below 0.3 across the board indicate the field's constraint has shifted from who writes code to who reviews it. Projects that invest in delegated triage, automated review, and maintainer expansion will outpace peers in the next 6 months.

  8. Stable releases are diverging from fixed code. OpenClaw's fixes locked in beta, ZeroClaw's release alongside red CI, and QwenPaw's regression-heavy 2.3.0 all point to a release-engineering gap across the ecosystem. Users increasingly ask "which version actually has the fix?" — a trust tax the category is paying collectively.

  • Guardrails punish legitimate work. #8184 and #8361 share a narrative: the framework's safety mechanisms (doom-loop gate, memory-search dedup) interrupt correct agent behavior and then fail to produce a valid reply. This erodes trust in long-running autonomous tasks.
  • Visual polish gaps (#8650, #8612, #8683) — repeatedly flagged as minor but persistent, especially for tablet/vertical layouts.

Satisfaction signals:

  • Very fast maintainer/contributor turnaround on well-scoped loop bugs (#8700 → #8701 same day).
  • Console/UX enhancements from users are being implemented and closed (#8605, #8663, #8650, #8612).

Use cases observed: multi-workspace Matrix deployments, WeChat channel operation, cron-driven scheduled agents, local Whisper transcription, document (Office COM) automation, and long-horizon background-task polling.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention — long-open, high-impact, or without fix PRs:

  • #8695 [OPEN] — Same-host reverse proxy auth bypass (2.3.0) — Security. No fix PR. Highest priority for triage.
  • #8184 [OPEN] — Doom-loop gate terminates legitimate polling (since 2026-10-12) — Open a month. Fix PR #8702 addresses the cron-status half, but the root gate-vs-polling distinction may need design discussion.
  • #8580 [OPEN] — Memory tag index never rebuilds (since 2026-11-04) — No fix PR; functional regression in memory subsystem.
  • #8018 [OPEN] [Under Review, size/XL] — Never write a sandbox ACE on a volume root — Open since 2026-09-29, still Under Review. Windows security-relevant.
  • #8048 [OPEN] [Under Review, size/M] — Guard inline Office COM automation before unsandboxed fallback — Same window as #8018; security-relevant, awaiting review.
  • #8236 [OPEN] [Under Review, size/XL] — Size Ollama context from num_ctx — Open since 2026-10-14; affects local-model users materially.

The recurring theme across the backlog is security-review latency: the auth bypass (#8695) is new and urgent, while two Windows sandbox-hardening PRs (#8018, #8048) have awaited review for six weeks.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-13

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw shows continued high velocity heading into the v0.9.0 release window, with 50 issues and 50 PRs updated in the last 24 hours and one major release published (v0.9.0). Activity is heavily weighted toward the security and multi-tenancy roadmap: filesystem sandbox policy (#6996), per-sender RBAC (#5982), and OIDC inbound authentication (#8289) dominate discussion. However, project health is currently degraded by two blocking CI/security problems — issue #12320 (RUSTSEC-2026-0459 libsqlite3-sys) is failing the Security job on every build, which blocks the merge queue entirely, and #7462 reports 74 test failures on Windows that CI does not catch. The merged-PR count (4) is low relative to 46 open PRs, and many long-running PRs (#10391, #9809, #11847) are marked needs-author-action or needs-maintainer-review, indicating a review bottleneck.

2. Releases

v0.9.0 — "First multi-user release"

Headline: The first release in which people other than the operator can sign in, spanning 117 commits from 22 contributors.

Key changes:

  • OpenID Connect sign-in for the dashboard via your own OIDC provider.
  • Scoped chats for non-admin accounts — users who aren't administrators get their own isolated chat scope.
  • This is a first multi-tenant / identity milestone, building on the tracker #8289 (OIDC milestone: canonical principals and inbound authentication) and #7432 (Runtime, dashboard sign-in and gateway delivery).

Migration / breaking-change notes: The release notes were truncated in the source data ("...an"), so full migration guidance could not be verified here. Operators upgrading from v0.8.x should review the full v0.9.0 changelog and the v0.9.1 milestone (#8358, #7432) before upgrading, particularly around auth/config schema changes.

Immediate post-release risk: v0.9.0 shipped while the Security CI job is red (#12320), meaning a v0.9.1 patch release is already effectively required — several issues are explicitly labeled release:v0.9.1 (#7432, #8289, #11580).

3. Project Progress

4 PRs were merged/closed in the last 24h (out of 50 updated). The data shows a merge-to-open ratio of roughly 1:11, reflecting a substantial review backlog rather than a lack of contributor interest.

Features advancing (still open, in review):

  • Inter-agent session tooling — #12258 sessions_prompt (sync inter-agent session prompting) and #12259 async sessions_message scaffold both authored by Audacity88, moving the agent-to-agent messaging roadmap forward.
  • Sandbox policy unification — #7821 canonical sandbox_policy schema with application-layer enforcement addresses the long-running drift described in #6996.
  • Goal Mode foundation — #11878 durable task lifecycle foundation [1/12] is the first slice of a 12-part Goal Mode proposal.
  • Multi-model provider profiles — #9809 support multiple models per provider profile (schema-v4 connections, fallback graphs).
  • New channels/providers — #11847 native Rust XMPP with optional legacy OMEMO and #12406 Parallel web search provider.

Closures: #11853 ci: npm audit failed — 2026-10-19 (Tailwind typography moderate advisory) was closed today, indicating the JS dependency audit path was remediated.

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment count (most active first):

Rank Item Comments Theme
1 #6996 RFC: Granular sandbox policy - filesystem restrictions 29 Security architecture
2 #7462 74 test failures on Windows 19 Cross-platform CI
3 #8396 RFC: Make wire protocol first-class in provider construction 19 Provider architecture
4 #7432 [Tracker]: Runtime, dashboard sign-in and gateway delivery 17 v0.9.x release coordination
5 #5937 refactor: Unify providers architecture and reqwest client management 12 Tech debt
6 #5982 Per-sender RBAC for multi-tenant agent deployments 12 Multi-tenancy

Underlying needs analysis:

  • Sandboxing and filesystem policy (#6996) is the single hottest topic, driven by a real architectural problem: two filesystem-policy layers that have historically drifted (application-layer path admission vs. OS sandbox backends like Bubblewrap/Landlock/Seatbelt). Users are asking for one authoritative policy model.
  • Provider architecture (#8396, #5937) reveals recurring dissatisfaction with inconsistent reqwest usage and fragmented provider config — contributors want a first-class wire-protocol abstraction.
  • Multi-tenancy (#5982, #7432, #8289) is the strategic theme of this release cycle: the community is converging on building sender roles on the existing agent/risk-profile model rather than a separate [rbac.*] subsystem.
  • Windows support (#7462) is a persistent, unresolved gap (no 👍 but high comment count = active debugging, not broad upvoting).

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (S0 highest):

Severity Issue Status Fix PR?
S0 #8279 delegate bypasses parent's tool allowlist — sub-agent can invoke tools the parent policy excludes accepted, p1 Related work in #10391
S1 #12320 Security job fails on every build: RUSTSEC-2026-0459 (libsqlite3-sys 0.38.2) open, release:v0.9.1 No fix PR yet — blocks merge queue
S1 #8794 [web dashboard] stopping agent mid-work erases tool calls and thinking from context accepted, p1 No
S1 #7462 74 Windows test failures (Unix-only commands, path semantics, cp936 console encoding) in-progress Related: #7461 CI matrix
S2 #6105 Agent lacks context of the cron job it ran in-progress No
S2 #8642 MCP/tool-schema cloning drives unbounded RSS growth accepted, help wanted No

Critical stability risks:

  1. #12320 is the most urgent item in the project — it fails CI Required Gate on every run, so "no pull request can merge and the merge queue can't land anything." This is a release-blocking dependency vulnerability in bundled SQLite.
  2. #8279 is a genuine S0 security regression: the delegate tool populates sub-agents with the unfiltered parent tool set, so a sub-agent can call tools the parent's policy explicitly excludes. This directly undermines the sandbox/RBAC model the project is otherwise investing heavily in.
  3. #8642 (memory growth / OOM) remains open and help wanted, split from the multi-root-cause tracker #5542 — no owner.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Most-likely-to-land-in-v0.9.1 / next cycle (based on release:v0.9.1 labels and active PRs):

  1. OIDC close-out (#8289) — core stack merged; remaining gap is canonical principals and enrollment migration. High confidence for v0.9.1.
  2. Runtime / dashboard sign-in / gateway delivery (#7432) — explicit v0.9.1 tracker.
  3. Release binary size gate resolution (#11580) — x86_64 Linux binary is ~0.7 MB (1%) under the 64 MiB hard cap; needs a headroom policy decision before next release.
  4. Subscription-native provider auth (#5601) — Ollama Cloud, Z.AI, Kimi Code, MiniMax; extends the existing OAuth/login pattern.
  5. Per-sender RBAC (#5982) — narrowed scope, builds on agent/risk-profile; draft PR #11068 exists.
  6. Unified capability catalog / "everything is a plugin" (#6489) — north-star product direction, longer horizon.
  7. Air-gapped execution mode (#6293) — blocked RFC; niche but security-critical.

Smaller feature requests with recent activity: per-skill security permissions (#5775), deterministic cron precondition gates (#5607), typed per-agent git identity (#8226), and TOTP for cross-channel critical-tool approval (#3767).

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points expressed by real users:

  • "My agent can't see what it just sent." (#6105) — when an agent sends a cron-triggered reminder, it has no reference to the message it produced, breaking conversational continuity.
  • "Stopping the agent erases its work." (#8794) — cancelling mid-turn drops all tool calls and reasoning from context as if the step never happened. Reported as S1 - workflow blocked.
  • "Delegation silently widens permissions." (#8279) — a security-conscious user found that a sub-agent can invoke tools the parent policy excludes, undermining their sandbox.
  • "My container OOMs when the LLM falls back to shell." (#6916) — observed in production where wkhtmltopdf consumed all memory; users want process-level memory caps on shell/skill subprocesses.
  • "Enabling one skill's permissions opens them for all." (#5775) — global allow_scripts/allowed_commands flags break least-privilege; users want per-skill scoping.
  • "Telegram replies to media lose the content." (#12405, #12197) — a user replying "summarize this" to a PDF gets nothing, because replies reduce quoted media to a bare [Document] marker.

Sentiment: Generally constructive and security-forward, but there is a clear pattern of frustration with multi-tenancy/sandboxing edge cases (delegation bypass, per-skill scoping, memory limits) and regression-like UX issues (context loss on stop, media reply handling). The community is clearly pushing ZeroClaw toward production multi-tenant deployment, which is exactly where several current gaps (RBAC, sandbox granularity, OIDC close-out) live.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention (long-open, high-impact, or blocked):

Blocked / stalled but important:

  • #6293 RFC: Air-gapped execution mode with companion daemon over unix socket — status:blocked, type:rfc. Enclave support is a strategic security capability with no clear unblock path.
  • #5869 security: rumqttc v0.25.1 pins vulnerable rustls-webpki — RUSTSEC cluster (0049/0098/0099/0104/0134) — status:blocked. Single transitive dep holding back TLS fixes; 5 comments and no resolution path.
  • #8519 Reconcile cargo-audit ignores and remediate wasmtime-wasi CVEs — p1, type:dependencies, .audit.toml/deny.toml drift.

Long-running high-value items:

  • #3767 require TOTP for cross-channel approval of critical tools — open since 2026-03-17, p1, security:policy. 8 months old with only 4 comments; needs a decision.
  • #5937 Unify providers architecture and reqwest client management — open since 2026-04-20, 12 comments, still status:accepted with no PR.
  • #6917 Honor action-scope filter in Composio tool dispatch — plus #6916 process-memory limits on shell subprocesses — both p1/p2 security, no fix PRs.
  • #7130 forbid(unsafe_code) workspace-wide with narrow reviewed unsafe boundaries — safety hardening, no PR.

PRs awaiting author/maintainer action:

  • #9809 multi-model provider profiles — open since 2026-08-07, needs-author-action, size:XL. High-value but stalled ~3 months.
  • #10391 keep bounded delegate's workspace/tool ceiling/command policy bound — the fix for S0 #8279 and #9872, open since 2026-08-26, needs-author-action. This is arguably the most important unmerged security fix in the repo.
